title: Computing & the Internet
tagline: From punched cards to the world wide web.

events.title: ENIAC is completed
events.text: The Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer, the first large general-purpose electronic computer, is unveiled at the University of Pennsylvania.

events.title: FORTRAN is released
events.text: IBM ships FORTRAN, the first widely used high-level programming language, making computers approachable for scientists and engineers.

events.title: ARPANET sends its first message
events.text: The ARPANET (predecessor of the internet) sends “LO” between UCLA and Stanford, the first data sent between two connected computers.

events.title: The first email is sent
events.text: Ray Tomlinson sends the first network email on ARPANET and popularises the @ symbol for addressing.

events.title: Apple I kicks off the PC era
events.text: Steve Wozniak and Steve Jobs release the Apple I, putting a personal computer in the hands of individuals rather than institutions.

events.title: The World Wide Web is invented
events.text: Tim Berners-Lee proposes the World Wide Web at CERN — a hypertext system that becomes the face of the internet.

references.label: CERN: the birth of the web

events.title: Mosaic makes the web visual
events.text: The Mosaic browser popularises images inside web pages, transforming the web from text-only to the graphical internet.

references.label: History of the web browser — Wikipedia

events.title: Google is founded
events.text: Larry Page and Sergey Brin found Google, whose PageRank algorithm revamps web search and defines the commercial internet.

events.title: The iPhone arrives
events.text: Apple introduces the iPhone, ushering in the smartphone era and permanently changing how people access the internet.

events.title: Bitcoin creates decentralised internet money
events.text: The Bitcoin network launches, introducing blockchain and a cryptocurrency that does not depend on banks or the state.
